tasks.short: Deliver orders to the kitchen and serve ready food

steps.what: Check the completed order ticket and its kitchen destination
Deliver the checked orders to the kitchen preparation station
Collect the ready food from the kitchen service area
Match collected food to the order and check service readiness
Serve the checked food to the correct customer

tasks.design: Enable native kitchen-ticket routing in {OTHER}, the point-of-sale and kitchen-display system, where tickets are currently carried by hand. Retain the worker's final ticket check, physical pickup, food matching and customer service.
tasks.previous_blocker: Hand-carried order tickets interrupt counter service.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing till software can route the checked order to its preparation station.
tasks.still_hard: Food readiness, completeness and safe physical handover remain situational.
tasks.human_edge: The worker matches the actual prepared food to the customer.
tasks.altitude: Avoid ticket-carrying trips while retaining food service.

evidence.claim: Lightspeed Order Anywhere routes orders to the bar or kitchen through the POS; this supports native order routing, not automated food pickup.
Ticket-carrying time and savings are unmeasured local assumptions.

assumptions: Order conversation and ticket creation belong to task23119 and are priced there; this task starts with its completed ticket and includes the actual kitchen send. No labour saving is counted twice.

The counter worker produces item identifiers, quantities, modifiers and order reference during ticket writing in23119. In this task s1 counts the final destination/version check. Missing fields return to the retained ticket-entry process; no free structured order is assumed.
OTHER is the point-of-sale/kitchen-display category. Native routing removes15 hours of actual hand-carrying only; if routing is already active, its runtime earns no new saving.
There is no automated ready alert or service-completion record. Pickup is prompted by the kitchen's existing ready-food practice and all associated checking remains.
unknowns: Whether preparation stations support native routing
research_questions: Does a shift trial eliminate actual ticket trips without creating missed or duplicated kitchen orders?

already_counted.description: Final ticket check and food readiness/matching remain in s1 and s4.

incremental.description: Counter worker checks routing after station changes.

approvals.approved_version: Exact order reference, items, quantities, modifiers and destination station checked in s1; edits invalidate approval and stop routing.
Actual prepared food, order reference and receiving customer checked immediately before handover; changed items require a renewed check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 B100 R85, gross15 less upkeep1 gives net14. Low0 retains the current process when native routing is already active and no change is adopted. High10 retains four hours of hand delivery for stations without displays plus85 other hours: R89, net10 after upkeep1. Central assumes every current ticket-carrying trip can be replaced; physical food work is never reduced.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Find current work procedures and training references
Prepare the training material and local examples for employees
Supervise employees and adjust guidance to current service conditions
Train employees through explanation and demonstration of the work
Observe employee practice and correct errors or unsafe handling

tasks.design: Use a current-procedure index and reusable sections of existing training material in {DOCS}. The worker still supervises, teaches and observes employees directly; no completion log is added where one is not kept today.
tasks.previous_blocker: Finding references and recreating standard teaching sections add preparation work.
tasks.enabler_now: Native document indexing and reusable sections remove specific clerical preparation.
tasks.still_hard: Food handling and service practice need live observation and correction.
tasks.human_edge: The trainer sees when an employee has misunderstood the task.
tasks.altitude: Prepare existing training material faster without changing supervisory responsibility.

evidence.claim: Document indexing and reusable teaching sections may shorten preparation; the task-specific saving is unmeasured.

assumptions: This counter-worker task covers the typical delegated supervising/training activity, including its actual teaching material. It does not invent hiring, appraisal or routine coaching records.

The procedure owner produces current procedures through existing work. The counter worker identifies learner needs and checks procedure applicability in s1/s2, retaining capture and local adaptation. Missing revisions require manual checking.
An index removes two of10 reference hours. Reusable standard sections remove4.5 of15 material-preparation hours;10.5 remain for real examples, checking and ordinary author saves without a gate.
Colleague instruction uses internal authority and no new approval stage. No machine publication or training-status send is proposed.
unknowns: Whether reusable training material already exists
research_questions: What preparation remains after selecting the actual local equipment and learner needs?

already_counted.description: Reference checking and material adaptation remain in s1 and s2.

incremental.description: Worker updates reused sections after procedure changes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 B100 R93.5, gross6.5 less upkeep1 gives net5.5. Low0 retains all preparation where suitable material is already available or teaching is wholly spontaneous and no configuration is adopted. High3 retains nine reference hours and12 material hours for partly reusable sections, plus75 interpersonal hours: R96, net3. Central retains eight reference and10.5 material hours.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Notify the kitchen of shortages and special orders

steps.what: Identify the actual shortage or clarify the special order with those involved
Write the shortage or special-order details on the existing kitchen message
Check the exception message and its intended kitchen station
Notify kitchen personnel with the checked shortage or special-order message
Confirm kitchen understanding and resolve any ambiguity in the request

tasks.design: Use native exception-message fields and kitchen routing in {OTHER}, the point-of-sale and kitchen-display system. The worker identifies and writes the exception, checks the exact message before routing and personally resolves kitchen questions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Separate handwritten or relayed exception messages can require a trip to the kitchen.
tasks.enabler_now: The existing kitchen channel can carry a checked order-linked exception.
tasks.still_hard: An unclear request or actual shortage needs human confirmation.
tasks.human_edge: The worker establishes what the customer or kitchen really means.
tasks.altitude: Deliver genuine exception messages without repeated relay trips.

evidence.claim: Lightspeed Order Anywhere supports POS-to-kitchen order routing; using a native exception field on that channel requires local validation.
Exception-message preparation and relay savings are unmeasured estimates.

assumptions: This task prices exception-specific content and its send. Normal item ticket creation belongs to23119 and routine kitchen delivery to23123; the same message is not counted twice.

The counter worker is the producer of item/order reference, exception type, actual shortage or special instruction and destination station. Observation is in s1, structured capture in s2 with16 retained hours, and final meaning checking in s3. No pre-existing sold-out flag or zero-cost shortage input is assumed.

Native message defaults remove four of20 repeated-context writing hours; routing removes25 relay hours. Kitchen clarification and actual exception writing remain. Missing references or unsupported exceptions use manual relay.
No automatic stock depletion, sold-out website update or extra alert is implied. This is the actual kitchen message already read today, not a new trailing log.
unknowns: Whether current exceptions already travel through the kitchen display
Which special instructions require spoken confirmation
research_questions: Can the native channel preserve the exact exception meaning and order reference without an additional relay?

already_counted.description: Exception identification, capture, checking and kitchen clarification remain in s1, s2, s3 and s5.

incremental.description: Worker checks exception fields and routing after menu or station changes.

approvals.approved_version: Exact item/order reference, exception instruction or shortage, timestamp and destination checked in s3; any change invalidates approval and stops routing.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 B100 R71, gross29 less upkeep1 gives net28. Low10 retains all20 writing hours and14 manual relay hours for unsupported special instructions, plus55 identification/checking/clarification hours: R89, net10. High20 retains18 writing and six manual relay hours with fewer unsupported exceptions, plus55 other hours: R79, net20. Central retains16 writing hours and no routine relay; actual meaning checks remain full.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Take orders, write tickets and give identifying stubs

steps.what: Take customers' orders and clarify the requested items and quantities
Write the ordered items and quantities on the order ticket
outputs: completed order ticket and identifying stub

steps.what: Read back the ticket and correct any mismatch with the customer's order
inputs: completed order ticket and identifying stub

steps.what: Check and give the identifying ticket stub to the customer

tasks.design: Configure menu buttons, common quantity controls and native ticket numbering in {OTHER}, the point-of-sale system. The worker takes the order, writes variable details, confirms the actual ticket and hands over its identifying stub; kitchen transmission is separately priced in23123.
tasks.previous_blocker: A poorly arranged till menu can require repeated searching and item entry.
tasks.enabler_now: Native menu controls can shorten specific entry operations without moving capture to customers.
tasks.still_hard: Unclear orders and changes require dialogue and correction.
tasks.human_edge: The worker clarifies and confirms what the customer wants.
tasks.altitude: Write actual tickets with fewer menu-navigation operations.

reach.learn: Which real orders require excessive entry steps

evidence.claim: Native till menu buttons and ticket identifiers are a plausible configuration; their task-specific entry saving is unmeasured.

assumptions: Order conversation, actual ticket writing, confirmation and stub handover are all included. No kiosk transfer, automatic customer ordering or payment step is assumed.

The worker produces the ordered item, quantity and normal modifier fields in s1 and captures them with order reference in s2. Menu staff maintain current item identifiers through existing work. All26 retained ticket hours include actual capture and correction; absent menu items require manual entry.

OTHER is the point-of-sale system. Native menu layout removes14 of40 navigation/repeated-selection hours, retaining26 hours for real item and quantity entry, ticket production and ordinary saving without self-approval.

No separate machine print action is added: native ticket numbering and existing printing are runtime already present today and earn no labour saving. The actual customer handover remains its own step.
unknowns: Whether native quick-entry controls already cover common orders
research_questions: How many item-entry operations disappear for actual menu combinations after configuration?

already_counted.description: Actual ticket capture and customer correction remain in s2 and s3.

incremental.description: Worker checks quick-entry controls after menu changes.

approvals.approved_version: Actual customer-facing question or menu statement checked for current item availability before speaking; changed requests require renewed checks.
Exact ticket items, quantities and normal modifiers read back from the actual version; corrections require renewed confirmation.
Exact stub/order identifier and receiving customer checked immediately before handover; a changed ticket invalidates the check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 B100 R86, gross14 less upkeep1 gives net13. Low0 retains all current ticket work when common orders already use native quick controls and no new configuration is adopted. High9 retains30 of40 ticket hours because several modifiers still require manual navigation, plus60 dialogue/confirmation/handover hours: R90, net9. Central retains26 ticket hours only where the current menu layout genuinely creates removable operations.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Keep customer service, food checking and employee teaching personal while reducing actual ticket entry and relay work.
reach: Kitchen staff receiving precise exception messages
role.ambitious_version: A counter worker who can keep orders moving with fewer relay trips while retaining clear customer and kitchen communication.
